description:
Scope: test-only coverage plan for lib/zaq/engine/history/delivery.ex; do not alter production code or existing tests. Exclusive owned test path: test/zaq/engine/history/delivery_test.exs (new). Existing test/zaq/engine/scoped_channel_rating_test.exs proves stored/conflict paths, and test/zaq/engine/history_ingress_test.exs lines 765+ supplies a model for replicated fixtures, but their private helpers cannot be imported. Preserve transport success even when history association fails. No feature E2E: this is an Engine internal contract already observable via DB integration tests. Action reuse: not applicable; no operation is designed or changed, only tests of existing Delivery/HistoryIngress public entrypoints. Documentation changes: none; this issue is the durable plan.

Tests to write before any implementation, all through Delivery.capture/2 or /3:
1. L25: construct %Outgoing{body: "reply", provider: :mattermost, channel_id: "room", routing_context: %{channel_config_id: positive_id, conversation_type: nil}, metadata: %{user_message_id: "u", assistant_message_id: "a"}} and {:ok, %{confirmation: :confirmed, message_id: "remote"}}. Assert exact original {:ok, receipt} unchanged, no history_capture key or DB insert. Use a real persisted retrieval ChannelConfig ID to avoid a false positive from the guard. Also test unknown conversation_type/hint cannot force history capture; property assessment below.
2. L61: create real enabled retrieval ChannelConfig(provider: "email:imap"), two People with distinct email channel identities (use People.create_person/1 + People.add_channel/1 as in history_ingress_test.exs:589-629), then recipient-addressed %Outgoing{provider: :"email:imap", channel_id: "old-thread", body: "sent", routing_context: %{channel_config_id: config.id, conversation_type: :recipient_addressed, source_scope: "smtp:confirmed"}, metadata: %{}}. Confirm with receipt %{confirmation: :confirmed, message_id: "sent-id", audience: %{platform: "email", sender: "system@example.com", recipients: ["first@example.com", "later@example.com"]}}. Assert {:ok, %{history_capture: :stored}}, persisted Message external id/content and transcript/message association for first recipient only, not second; original outgoing.channel_id intentionally differs to distinguish the head-of-recipients path. Follow actual person/transcript query helpers from history_ingress_test.exs and assert source identity/config to prevent a false pass. Replicated mode bypasses the two-ID guard even with empty metadata.
3. L72: valid config and direct/room Outgoing with both binary metadata IDs, receipt confirmed but source_scope set to a non-JSON-encodable value (e.g. self() PID), so HistoryIngress.record_confirmation/1 raises at Jason.encode! of advisory-lock arguments inside the rescued association_status/1. Assert {:ok, %{history_capture: :unavailable, history_capture_error: :history_capture_unavailable}} with original confirmation/message_id retained, no successful Message/TranscriptMessage association and no Oban job. The :history_capture_failed reason is deliberately sanitized by unavailable/1. Verify PID really triggers that exact rescued path before relying on this test; if not, find another deterministic bad receipt field consumed by Jason inside HistoryIngress, not a global DB outage or an internal mock.
4. L69: catch-all branch requires HistoryIngress.capture_confirmed/1 to return something other than {:ok, _} or {:error, _}. Its current public implementation calls record_confirmation/1 then associate_confirmation/1, both returning tagged tuples; no safe normal input seems to reach L69. Mark uncovered as contract-defensive unless a real collaborator return path is found. Do not monkey-patch HistoryIngress or add a test-only callback merely for the metric.
5. L74: catch :exit requires a real HistoryIngress process exit during confirmation. No injectable collaborator is used (capture_kind/4 ignores opts), and inducing Repo/sandbox or global supervisor failure is unsafe and timing-dependent. Mark as blocked by absence of a production-meaningful controlled exit boundary; only revisit if a genuinely reproducible isolated real-world exit case exists. Never kill shared Repo, change global env/Mox mode, or weaken assertions to hit it.

Isolation/fixtures/mocks: use Zaq.DataCase sandbox; begin async: true if all cases have per-test DB ownership and Oban operation is sandbox-safe; use dedicated async: false module only if investigation demonstrates shared process/global state. Use unique config names and message IDs per test, and explicit local constructors for Outgoing/receipts. Reuse existing public People, ChannelConfig changeset, Repo and canonical history read/query patterns; no external network, sleeps, polling or Mox/internal mocks. For the replicated case observe committed state synchronously after capture; assert exact receipt and durable per-recipient association. For the exception case assert non-resend semantics and no persistent side effects.

Property assessment: guard/permission-default invariant is relevant. Add a bounded StreamData property over unsupported conversation_type values (e.g. nil, :unknown, :broadcast) with otherwise valid confirmed receipts and a valid config, asserting the unchanged receipt and no capture keys; do not generate arbitrary malformed structs or run DB-heavy replicated properties for this finite selection. A focused example remains required. No useful property for rare exceptional/catch-all branches.

Validation for implementer, not this planning task: run focused `mix test test/zaq/engine/history/delivery_test.exs` in isolation and `mix q` via Context Mode (includes formatting), inspect coverage of exactly lines 25/61/69/72/74 with a fresh coverage report during the authorized coverage phase; do not claim lines 69/74 covered without execution evidence. If impossible, report blocked lines with reasons in issue/PR and do not mutate production solely for coverage. Later final gate `mix precommit` only per workflow after review/coverage completion. No Git commits/pushes under this plan.

comments.text: Correction to scenario 2: replicated confirmation fans out to ALL linked audience recipients (HistoryIngress.delivery_facts/2 lines 397-417), not only the head. Assert both first and later recipient histories contain the message, and an unrelated non-recipient has no copy. To prove delivery_channel_id/3 selected first recipient rather than outgoing.channel_id, inspect the persisted confirmation fingerprint/derived source identity or provoke a second confirmation with same external message ID but a changed outgoing.channel_id and assert idempotence; only use an assertion backed by the actual stored contract. Prefer inspect the canonical message metadata/history source identity before specifying the precise assertion. Do not assert second recipient exclusion.
